title: Is all-time-high proximity a universal/sourcing signal, or only real within the existing shortlist?

tables.name: Near-ATH vs baseline win rate, by accumulation-rank tier (fresh window=10d)

notes: EXCLUDED = tickers the accumulation shortlist never even considers (accumulation_rank > 50). If EXCLUDED shows a real, both-splits win-rate edge for near-ATH, that means the signal is genuinely independent of accumulation, not just riding along with it -- worth a harder look at using it to pull in tickers outside the current shortlist. If not, only worth using as a reranking factor within the existing top-50 (see ath_boost_calibration.py).

conclusion.summary: EXCLUDED tier shows no consistent near-ATH edge -- not a universal/sourcing signal. IMPORTANT: an earlier run of this script (2026-07-30, before classify_ath()'s lookahead-bias fix) showed the opposite -- a strong apparent edge across every tier. That was an artifact of using the trade day's own closing price as the reference point instead of the last price known before the decision. Trust only runs after the fix.
